items.title: Interior of the Earth — Layers & Discontinuities
items.body:
## Three-layer structure

- **Crust** — outermost, brittle. **Oceanic crust** = basaltic (SIMA), density ~3.0 g/cm³, mean 5 km, younger; **continental crust** = granitic (SIAL), density ~2.7 g/cm³, mean 30 km, older.
- **Mantle** — from the Moho to ~2900 km. The upper mantle includes the weak **asthenosphere** (to ~400 km), the source of magma. **Lithosphere** = crust + rigid upper mantle (10–200 km).
- **Core** — the **NIFE** layer (nickel + iron). **Outer core** is molten (~2200 km thick); **inner core** is solid (~1220 km).

## Discontinuities (top to bottom)

| Discontinuity | Separates |
|---|---|
| Conrad | Upper crust / lower crust |
| Mohorovicic (Moho) | Crust / mantle |
| Repetti | Upper mantle / lower mantle |
| Gutenberg | Lower mantle / outer core |
| Lehmann | Outer core / inner core |

## Sources & abundances

- Interior known from **seismic waves**, density, and temperature/pressure gradients (direct drilling reaches only a few km).
- **Oxygen** = most abundant element in the crust; **aluminium** = most abundant metal in the crust; **iron** = most abundant metal in the whole Earth.
keyPoints: Earth has three layers: crust, mantle (to ~2900 km) and core (NIFE = nickel + iron).
Oceanic crust = basaltic/denser/younger (~5 km); continental crust = granitic/thicker/older (~30 km).
Discontinuity order (mnemonic 'Commander Mohit is ReGuLar'): Conrad, Moho, Repetti, Gutenberg, Lehmann.
Moho separates crust from mantle; Gutenberg separates mantle from outer core.
Outer core is molten, inner core is solid; the asthenosphere is the source of magma.
Oxygen is the most abundant crustal element; iron is the most abundant metal in the whole Earth.
items.mnemonic: Discontinuities top-down: 'Commander Mohit is ReGuLar' = Conrad-Moho-Repetti-Gutenberg-Lehmann.
items.source: local APPSC GK PDF — Geomorphology: Interior of the Earth

figure.caption: Crust, mantle, liquid outer core and solid inner core; Moho and Gutenberg discontinuities.

items.title: From Continental Drift to Plate Tectonics
items.body:
## Evolution of the theory

- **Continental Drift (Alfred Wegener, 1922)** — a single supercontinent **Pangaea** in the ocean **Panthalassa**; the Tethys Sea split it into **Laurasia** (north) and **Gondwanaland** (south). Drift began ~200 million years ago.
  - Evidence: jigsaw fit of coastlines, **Glossopteris** flora, **Mesosaurus** fossils (S. Africa + Brazil), tillite and placer/gold deposits, matching rock belts.
  - Weakness: the driving forces Wegener proposed (buoyancy, tidal, gravity) were too weak.
- **Convection Current Theory (Arthur Holmes, 1930s)** — radioactive heat drives mantle convection.
- **Sea-Floor Spreading (Harry Hess)** — magma rises at diverging ridges, forming new crust that moves outward; proven by **paleomagnetic stripes** flipped symmetrically across ridges.
- **Plate Tectonics (McKenzie & Parker 1967; Morgan 1968)** — the lithosphere is broken into plates floating on the asthenosphere.

## Plates & boundaries

- **Seven major plates**: Pacific, North American, South American, Eurasian, African, Antarctic, Indo-Australian. Minor: Nazca, Cocos, Arabian, Philippine, Caribbean, Juan de Fuca.
- **Divergent** (constructive): mid-ocean ridges, East African Rift. **Convergent** (destructive): folding/trenches/subduction (Himalayan Boundary Fault). **Transform**: plates slide past — **San Andreas Fault**.

## The Indian Plate

- India began moving north ~200 mya, **collided with Asia 40–50 mya** raising the Himalayas (still rising). The same movement produced the **Deccan Traps** flood basalts (~60 mya).
keyPoints: Wegener (1922) proposed Continental Drift — Pangaea + Panthalassa, split by Tethys into Laurasia and Gondwanaland.
Drift evidence: coastline fit, Glossopteris flora, Mesosaurus fossils, tillite and placer deposits.
Harry Hess proposed sea-floor spreading; paleomagnetism is its key proof; Holmes proposed mantle convection.
Seven major plates; boundaries are divergent (ridges), convergent (trenches/mountains) or transform (San Andreas Fault).
The Indian plate collided with Asia 40-50 mya, uplifting the still-rising Himalayas and forming the Deccan Traps.
items.mnemonic: Boundary outcomes: Divergent = build (ridge), Convergent = crush (mountain/trench), Transform = slide (fault).

items.title: Earthquakes — Waves, Measurement & Distribution
items.body:
## Basics

- **Focus (hypocentre)** = where energy is released; **epicentre** = surface point directly above. **Foreshocks** precede, **aftershocks** follow; **swarms** are many small quakes without a main shock.
- Depth classes: **shallow** (0–70 km, ~70–85% of energy, most destructive), **intermediate** (70–300 km), **deep** (300–700 km).
- Causes: fault slip (tectonic), volcanic activity, and human-induced (mining, reservoirs — e.g. **Koynanagar 1967**).

## Seismic waves

| Wave | Nature | Medium | Speed / Destructiveness |
|---|---|---|---|
| P (primary) | Longitudinal/compressional | Solid, liquid, gas | Fastest, recorded first, least destructive |
| S (secondary) | Transverse/shear | Solids only | Medium; blocked by fluids (proves molten outer core) |
| L (surface) | Transverse, along surface | Surface | Slowest, recorded last, most destructive |

## Measurement & distribution

- **Richter scale (ML)** — energy; one step ≈ **32x** more energy, two steps ≈ **1,000x**. **Mercalli scale** — intensity (observed effects).
- **Circum-Pacific Belt (Ring of Fire)** ≈ 68% of quakes; **Alpine–Himalayan belt** ≈ 15% of energy; also mid-ocean ridge belts.
- India: **five seismic zones (II–V)**; **Zone V** highest risk (NE India, Himalayas, Kutch, Andaman-Nicobar). ~59% of India's area is at moderate-to-severe risk.
keyPoints: Focus = energy release point; epicentre = surface point above it; shallow quakes are the most destructive.
P-waves travel through all media and are fastest; S-waves cannot pass through liquids (proving a molten outer core).
Surface (L) waves are slowest but most destructive.
Richter scale: one step ≈ 32x energy, two steps ≈ 1,000x; Mercalli measures intensity/effects.
Ring of Fire ≈ 68% of earthquakes; Zone V is India's highest seismic-risk zone.
items.mnemonic: Wave order recorded = P then S then L (fast to slow); destructiveness is the reverse (L > S > P).
items.source: local APPSC GK PDF — Geomorphology: Earthquake

items.title: Volcanoes & Rocks
items.body:
## Volcano types

- **Shield** — broad, gentle slopes, fluid basaltic lava, largest, low explosivity (Mauna Loa).
- **Composite (stratovolcano)** — steep cone of alternating viscous lava/ash/tephra, Ring of Fire (Fuji, Vesuvius, Etna).
- **Caldera** — collapse depression after a huge eruption, most explosive (Yellowstone; Crater Lake).
- **Flood basalt** — vast outpourings of fluid lava (**Deccan Traps**).
- **Intrusive landforms**: batholith (largest), dyke (vertical), sill (horizontal), laccolith (dome), volcanic neck. **Extrusive**: cones, craters, lava domes, volcanic islands.

## Rock groups

| Group | Formation | Traits | Examples |
|---|---|---|---|
| Igneous (primary) | Cooling of magma/lava | Un-fossiliferous | Granite (plutonic), Basalt (extrusive) |
| Sedimentary | Lithification of sediments | Stratified, fossiliferous | Sandstone, shale, limestone, coal |
| Metamorphic | Heat/pressure recrystallisation | Foliation | Gneiss, slate, schist, marble, quartzite |

- **Metamorphism**: limestone→marble, sandstone→quartzite, coal→graphite/anthracite, granite→gneiss, clay/shale→slate/schist.
- **Rock cycle**: igneous rocks are primary; all three types can transform into one another; subduction remelts crust into magma.
keyPoints: Shield volcanoes (fluid basalt, gentle, e.g. Mauna Loa) vs composite (viscous, steep, e.g. Fuji) vs caldera (most explosive).
Deccan Traps are a flood-basalt province of highly fluid lava.
Intrusive landforms: batholith (largest), dyke (vertical), sill (horizontal), laccolith (dome).
Three rock groups: igneous (primary, un-fossiliferous), sedimentary (stratified/fossiliferous), metamorphic (foliated).
Metamorphism pairs: limestone→marble, sandstone→quartzite, coal→graphite, granite→gneiss.
Feldspar and quartz are the commonest rock-forming minerals; feldspar makes up ~half the crust.
items.mnemonic: Explosivity rises with lava thickness: Shield (thin/calm) < Composite < Caldera (thick/violent).
items.source: local APPSC GK PDF — Geomorphology: Volcano; Geomorphology: Rocks

items.title: Geological Time Scale & Earth-shaping Forces
items.body:
## Geological time scale

- Hierarchy: **Eon > Era > Period > Epoch**. Earth is ~**4.6 billion years** old.
- Key markers: Cambrian (~505–570 mya, marine invertebrates, no land life) → Carboniferous (coal beds, first reptiles) → **Permian** ends with mass extinction → **Jurassic** = Age of Dinosaurs → **Cretaceous** ends with dinosaur extinction (~65 mya) → Quaternary (Pleistocene = rise of Homo sapiens; **Holocene** = modern man).

## Endogenic vs exogenic forces

- **Endogenic (internal)** — powered by internal heat (mostly radioactive decay) and convection currents; build up the surface.
  - **Diastrophism**: **epeirogeny** (broad continental uplift/warping) and **orogeny** (mountain building by folding/faulting). Sudden movements = earthquakes and volcanic eruptions.
- **Exogenic (external)** — powered by **solar energy**; wear down the surface (**denudation** = weathering + erosion).
  - **Weathering** (in-situ breakdown): physical (exfoliation, frost, salt), chemical (carbonation, hydration, hydrolysis, oxidation), biological.
  - **Erosion** — removal/transport by water, wind, ice, waves.
- **Mountain types**: fold, block (faulting), volcanic, residual (erosional remnant).
- **W. M. Davis** founded the science of geomorphology.
keyPoints: Time-scale hierarchy: Eon > Era > Period > Epoch; Earth is ~4.6 billion years old.
Dinosaurs dominated in the Jurassic and went extinct at the end of the Cretaceous (~65 mya).
Endogenic forces (internal heat) build up the surface; exogenic forces (solar energy) wear it down.
Diastrophism = epeirogeny (broad uplift) + orogeny (mountain building by folding/faulting).
Denudation = weathering (in-situ breakdown) + erosion (removal); weathering is physical, chemical or biological.
Mountain types: fold, block, volcanic and residual.
items.mnemonic: ENDOgenic = ENergy from Deep (internal, builds up); EXOgenic = EXternal Sun (wears down).
items.source: local APPSC GK PDF — Geological Time Scale; Geomorphology: Introduction

items.title: Landforms of External Agents (River, Glacier, Wind, Karst, Sea)
items.body:
## Fluvial (river)

- Youth: **V-shaped valley, gorge, canyon, waterfalls, potholes**. Maturity: **meanders, oxbow lakes** (Kanwar Lake = largest in India). Old age: **delta, natural levees, alluvial fans, braided channels** (Majuli = world's largest river island).
- **Delta types**: arcuate (Ganga, Nile), bird's-foot (Mississippi), cuspate (Tiber), estuarine (Narmada, Tapi).

## Glacial

- Erosional: **cirque** (holds a tarn), **glacial trough (U-valley)**, **hanging valley**, **arete**, **horn**, **fjord**. Depositional: **moraine, esker, drumlin, kettle hole, outwash plain**. Siachen (Karakoram) is India's largest glacier.

## Arid / aeolian

- Erosional: **yardang, zeugen, inselberg, mushroom rock, deflation basin (blowout)**. Depositional: **sand dunes** (barchan = crescent, tips downwind; seif, star, parabolic), ripple marks, **loess** (fertile wind-blown silt). Playas = temporary desert lakes in bolsons.

## Karst (limestone)

- Carbonic acid dissolves limestone/dolomite: **sinkholes/swallow holes, dolines, uvalas, poljes, caves**, and dripstone **stalactites (ceiling) & stalagmites (floor)** that merge into pillars. Little surface drainage. (Named after the Karst region, Balkans.)

## Marine / coastal

- Erosional: **chasm, wave-cut platform, sea cave, sea arch, stack**. Depositional: **beach, bar, lagoon, spit, hook, tombolo** (links island to mainland). Submergence forms **ria** and **fjord** coasts.
keyPoints: Fluvial: V-valley/gorge/waterfall (youth) → meander/oxbow lake (maturity) → delta/levee (old age).
Delta types: arcuate (Ganga), bird's-foot (Mississippi), cuspate (Tiber), estuarine (Narmada/Tapi).
Glacial erosional: cirque, U-valley, arete, horn, fjord; depositional: moraine, esker, drumlin.
Barchan dunes are crescent-shaped with tips pointing downwind; loess is fertile wind-blown silt.
Karst (limestone dissolution): sinkholes, poljes, caves, stalactites (ceiling) and stalagmites (floor).
Marine: wave-cut platform, sea arch and stack (erosional); spit, lagoon and tombolo (depositional).

items.title: Indian Rock Systems, Minerals, Shale Gas & Barren Island
items.body:
Prelims frequently pairs a **rock system** with its characteristic **minerals**, and tests India's only active volcano.

## Rock systems and their minerals

| System | Age | Characteristic minerals |
|---|---|---|
| **Dharwar** | Oldest metamorphosed sediments | Metallic — **iron, manganese, gold (Kolar), copper** |
| **Cuddapah** | Proterozoic | Iron, manganese, limestone, asbestos, barytes |
| **Gondwana** | ~Carbon./Permian | **Coal (~98% of India's coal)**, sandstone |
| **Tertiary** | Cenozoic | **Petroleum**, younger (lignite) coal in NE India |

- **Kodarma (Jharkhand)** is India's **mica** belt.
- Trap: the **Dharwar** system is NOT a petroleum source — petroleum is **Tertiary**.

## Shale gas

- **Shale gas** = natural gas trapped in fine-grained **sedimentary shale**, freed by hydraulic fracturing.
- India's shale basins: **Cambay, Krishna-Godavari, Cauvery**, Gondwana, Assam-Arakan, Indo-Gangetic.

## Barren Island

- **India's only active volcano**, in the **Andaman Sea** (Andaman subduction arc) — NOT near Great Nicobar.
- Erupted repeatedly **after 1991** (e.g. 2017), so it is not dormant; **Narcondam** nearby is regarded as dormant.
keyPoints: Dharwar system = oldest metamorphosed rocks, rich in metallic minerals (iron, manganese, gold) — NOT petroleum.
Gondwana rocks hold ~98% of India's coal; petroleum comes from Tertiary rocks; Kodarma (Jharkhand) is the mica belt.
Shale gas occurs in the Cambay, Krishna-Godavari and Cauvery sedimentary basins.
Barren Island (Andaman Sea) is India's only active volcano and has erupted after 1991 (not dormant).
Narcondam is India's other volcanic island and is regarded as dormant.
items.mnemonic: Coal = Gondwana, Oil = Tertiary, Metals = Dharwar, Mica = Kodarma.
items.source: UPSC CSE Prelims 2013/2015/2018; Geological Survey of India; Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas
